$comment: Canonical Microsoft Sentinel scheduled-analytics-rule definitions for the
This file is the single source of truth. sentinel-analytic-rules.bicep
deploys it verbatim via loadJsonContent(), and
against backend/app/services/sentinel_schema.py — so a rule can never
reference a column the forwarder does not emit. That is the failure this
arrangement exists to prevent: such a rule deploys cleanly, never fires,
and the SOC silently believes it is covered.
Thresholds are the spec's proposed defaults (§8, open question 5) and are
declared as `let` statements at the top of each query so a customer can
tune them in the portal without rewriting the logic. They await security-PM

rules.description: A Prompt Shields event was recorded at High severity: sensitive data was blocked, redacted, or flagged on its way into an AI tool. This is the catch-all that puts every high-severity event into the analyst queue, so the SOC sees them without writing a detection rule first. Prompt content is never included — pivot on PromptHash to correlate the same prompt across events.
rules.query:
PromptShieldsActivity_CL
| where Severity == "High"
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    EventId,
    User,
    UserAadObjectId,
    Department,
    AiTool,
    IsShadowAi,
    EventType,
    SensitiveType,
    Detail,
    EndpointId,
    EndpointPlatform,
    PromptHash

rules.displayName: Prompt Shields — Repeated blocked prompts of the same sensitive type
rules.description: One person was blocked three or more times within an hour trying to put the same class of sensitive data into an AI tool. A single block is a policy working as intended; a burst is someone actively trying to get data out, or someone who does not understand the policy and needs a conversation. Tune AttemptThreshold and LookbackWindow in the query.
rules.query:
let LookbackWindow = 1h;
let AttemptThreshold = 3;
PromptShieldsActivity_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where EventType == "Blocked"
| where isnotempty(SensitiveType)
| summarize
    Attempts = count(),
    Tools = make_set(AiTool, 10),
    FirstAttempt = min(TimeGenerated),
    TimeGenerated = max(TimeGenerated),
    UserAadObjectId = any(UserAadObjectId),
    Department = any(Department)
    by User, SensitiveType
| where Attempts >= AttemptThreshold

rules.displayName: Prompt Shields — New shadow AI tool in use
rules.description: An unsanctioned AI tool appeared that has not been seen anywhere in the tenant during the baseline window. This is the shadow-AI early warning: a tool with no use case registered against it is being fed real work. BaselineWindow is capped at 14 days because that is Sentinel's maximum queryPeriod for a scheduled rule.
rules.query:
let BaselineWindow = 14d;
let DetectionWindow = 1d;
let KnownTools = PromptShieldsActivity_CL
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(BaselineWindow) .. ago(DetectionWindow))
    | distinct AiTool;
PromptShieldsActivity_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(DetectionWindow)
| where IsShadowAi
| where AiTool !in (KnownTools)
| summarize
    Events = count(),
    TimeGenerated = min(TimeGenerated),
    UserAadObjectId = any(UserAadObjectId),
    Department = any(Department),
    SensitiveTypes = make_set(SensitiveType, 10)
    by AiTool, User

rules.description: A prompt referencing protected characteristics was flagged — typically candidate screening, performance review, or benefits eligibility routed through an AI tool. This is an AI-governance signal rather than an intrusion, so no MITRE tactic is asserted: mapping it to one would misrepresent it in ATT&CK coverage reporting. Route it to whoever owns responsible-AI policy, not only to the SOC.
rules.query:
PromptShieldsActivity_CL
| where EventType == "BiasFlagged"
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    EventId,
    User,
    UserAadObjectId,
    Department,
    AiTool,
    SensitiveType,
    Severity,
    Detail
